title: Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup
description: Shin braised for three hours in a broth built on fermented broad bean paste, tomatoes and whole spice. The bowl is assembled at the last minute so the noodles never sit in the soup.
notes: There is a clear-broth camp and a red-braised camp, and this is firmly the second. The tomatoes are not a shortcut — they thin the bean paste and give the broth a sweetness that sugar alone cannot.

ingredients.name: beef shin
ingredients.note: cut into large chunks, sinew left on

ingredients.name: wheat noodles
ingredients.note: thick and chewy, not thin egg noodles

steps.text: Cover the beef shin with cold water in a large pot, bring it to a boil, then tip the whole lot into the sink. Rinse the meat and scrub the pot.
steps.tip: This blanch is not optional. It takes out the grey scum that would otherwise cloud the broth for the next three hours.

steps.text: Melt the beef tallow in the dry pot and fry the doubanjiang over a low flame until the fat runs red and the paste smells toasted rather than sharp.
steps.tip: Low and slow. Scorched bean paste tastes of ash and there is no rescuing the pot once it does.

steps.text: Add the onion, garlic, ginger, scallions and tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes have collapsed into the paste.
Return the beef, pour in the Shaoxing wine and soy sauce, and add the rock sugar, star anise, cinnamon, bay leaves and Sichuan peppercorns.
Pour in the water, bring it up to a bare simmer, and leave it barely moving until a spoon goes through the shin without resistance.
steps.tip: A rolling boil emulsifies the fat and turns the broth cloudy for good. You want the surface to shiver, not bubble.

steps.text: Fish out the aromatics and the whole spices, then taste and correct for salt and sweetness.
Boil the wheat noodles in a separate pot of water and drop the baby bok choy in for the final minute.
steps.tip: Never cook the noodles in the broth. The starch they shed turns three hours of work gluey.

steps.text: Divide the noodles between deep bowls, ladle over the broth and beef, and finish with pickled mustard greens, coriander and a spoonful of chilli oil.
